name: Relabel a reviewed head in CI

pr.title: Put the clean label back when project review run refuses a head already reviewed clean, such as one a force-push returned to
pr.head: 8b43f9396c043fc48b78bcc672daa9046966598a

summary: Projector marks a pull request with the clean label when its current head is signed off, meaning the newest Projector verdict on that commit is clean and no finding thread is open. Until now only project review publish added the label, at the end of a review. In CI, project review run starts an agent to review each new head, and it refuses a head that this model has already reviewed, so a rerun posts nothing.

Those two rules leave a gap. Suppose a branch is force-pushed away from a commit that was reviewed clean and then back to it. The first push takes clean off, correctly. On the second push, the CI run refuses the commit as already reviewed, so no publish runs and nothing puts the label back. The pull request looks unreviewed until someone forces a full rereview.

This change makes that one refusal re-sync the label before it exits 0. The run adds clean when the head is signed off and removes a stale clean when it is not. It decides with the code publish uses, which this change moves into two shared helpers, so the two paths cannot disagree.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Signed off: the newest counted Projector verdict on the head is clean and no finding thread is open.
  • Refusal: project review run exits 0 without starting an agent, as for a draft, a fork, a closed pull request, or a head this model already reviewed.
  • review.reviewers: extra logins whose verdicts count, such as the account a CI review posts as.

cards.title: What stays as it was
cards.html:
• The reviewing label: the refusal never adds or removes it.
  • The projector/review commit status: it belongs to the commit and is still on it.
  • The draft, closed, merged, and fork refusals: they change no label.
  • review.labels = false turns the re-sync off.

groups.title: Sign-off and labels shared with publish
groups.kicker: Two helpers lifted out of publish, plus the entry point the run calls
intro: publish used to work out the sign-off and edit the labels inline. This group moves both steps into functions, so the CI run can make exactly the same decision without running a review.

head_sign_off lists every counted verdict on the pull request and the open finding threads, then asks sign_off whether the head is signed off. label_sign_off adds or removes clean to match. If it added the label, it reads the head again and takes clean back off when a push landed during the edit. relabel_head is the run's entry point: it calls both and turns any failed read into a warning.

checks.text: I read the old inline publish code against the new calls. They behave the same: the review just posted is still dropped from the listing by id and added back, and the reviewing removal now comes in through remove.

files.note: Adds head_sign_off, label_sign_off, and relabel_head, and has publish call the first two.

checks.text: A review passed as posted counts even when GitHub's review listing does not show it yet. Only publish passes it.
The re-read after adding clean is the existing guard against a push that lands during the edit, moved here unchanged.

Every failure from reading the verdicts, the threads, or the reviewer's token is a ReviewError, which this function catches and turns into a warning. change_labels already returns a refused edit as a warning, so a re-sync never fails the run.

groups.title: The run's refusal re-syncs the label
groups.kicker: Where project review run calls the new helper, and how review.reviewers reaches it
intro: run checks for the other refusals first, then checks whether this model already reviewed the head. Only that last refusal calls relabel_head, and only while labels are on. The CLI now passes the logins from review.reviewers as also, so a teammate's or a CI account's verdict counts here as it does in publish.

files.note: Calls relabel_head after the already-reviewed refusal prints its reason, and still returns 0.

checks.text: refusal runs earlier and returns for a closed, fork, or draft pull request, so none of those reaches this line.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Four run tests against a fake GitHub that now serves review threads
intro: The fake gh in tests/test_run.py now answers the GraphQL thread query, so census can run inside it. The new tests cover four cases: a clean head gets clean back, an open finding takes a stale clean off, review.labels = false makes no edit, and a draft refusal makes no edit.

checks.text: The check workflow, which runs the whole test suite, passed on this head. project review gate also passed locally.

groups.title: Documentation and plan
groups.kicker: The CLI reference, the CI guide, the plugin panel, and the plan's decision list
intro: The CLI reference describes the re-sync and its output. The CI guide and the plugin page say that the run can put clean back. The plan review-in-ci is in-progress, and this change adds the decision to its list of fixes.

files.note: Adds run to the commands review.labels governs, and a section on the refusal's re-sync.

checks.text: The review.reviewers row in the settings table does not list run among the commands that read it. The review left this as a suggestion.
